title: Geometry columns from DuckDB to sf
text: DuckDB writes query result GeoParquet, CRS file. ten thousand random points Iberia, WGS 84 longitude latitude. geo_parquet_info() reads footer nothing else: row count, encoding, CRS DuckDB stored, box column’s statistics. geo_read_parquet() gives data frame whose geometry column geo_vctr, CRS taken file.
code: path <- tempfile(fileext = ".parquet") invisible(DBI::dbExecute(con, "SELECT setseed(0.42)")) invisible(DBI::dbExecute(con, sprintf("   COPY (     SELECT i AS id,            ST_SetCRS(ST_Point(-9.5 + random() * 12.5, 36 + random() * 7.8),                      'OGC:CRS84') AS geometry     FROM range(10000) t(i)   ) TO '%s' (FORMAT parquet, GEOPARQUET_VERSION 'BOTH')", path))) geo_parquet_info(path) #> <zugeo_parquet_info: 10,000 rows in 1 row groups; GeoParquet 1.0.0> #> * geometry: WKB GEOMETRY; Point; crs projjson: WGS 84 (CRS84); edges planar; bbox [-9.49522715809373 36.0000097816499, 2.99996306555653 43.7997633161704] df <- geo_read_parquet(path) head(df, 3) #>   id                                      geometry #> 1  0 POINT (-0.1599482076109382 39.44579523739312) #> 2  1 POINT (-1.0796949709503902 38.57168598702719) #> 3  2 POINT (-1.9511585203605986 39.79967235830755) geo_crs(df$geometry) #> <zugeo_crs projjson: WGS 84 (CRS84)>

text: geo_vctr reads WKT WKB keeps CRS beside geometries. Coordinates come back exactly went , encoding. R-tree finds intersects box. bytes flatbush’s format, magic byte fb first, flatbush JavaScript geo-index Python load unchanged. Lines sphere planar box, asking one error. qio installed, data frame geometries becomes GeoParquet. Reading bbox skips row groups whose statistics miss box, keeps rows meet . Every function prefixed geo_, apart zugeo_info(). zugeo’s errors inherit zugeo_error, class kind, zugeo_edges_error zugeo_crs_error.
code: library(zugeo) cities <- geo_vctr(   c("POINT (-9.139 38.722)", "POINT (-8.611 41.150)", "POINT (2.352 48.857)"),   crs = "OGC:CRS84" ) cities #> <geo_vctr[3] geoarrow.wkt wkt; crs authority_code; edges planar> #> [1] POINT (-9.139 38.722) #> [2] POINT (-8.611 41.150) #> [3] POINT (2.352 48.857) x <- geo_points(0.1 + 0.2, 1 / 3) cat(geo_as_wkt(x)) #> POINT (0.30000000000000004 0.3333333333333333) identical(geo_coords(geo_vctr(geo_as_wkb(x)))$x, 0.1 + 0.2) #> [1] TRUE tree <- geo_rtree(cities) geo_query_box(tree, geo_extent(-10, 38, -8, 42, crs = "OGC:CRS84")) #> [1] 1 2 geo_index_raw(tree)[1:2] #> [1] fb 38 route <- geo_vctr("LINESTRING (-9.139 38.722, 2.352 48.857)",   crs = "OGC:CRS84", edges = "spherical" ) geo_box(route) #> Error in `geo_box()`: #> ! A planar box can be wrong for "spherical" edges, which may bulge past their vertices or cross the antimeridian. Pass `lossy = "warn"` or `"allow"` for the planar box anyway. path <- tempfile(fileext = ".parquet") df <- data.frame(name = c("Lisbon", "Porto", "Paris")) df$geometry <- cities geo_write_parquet(df, path) geo_read_parquet(path, bbox = c(-10, 38, -8, 42)) #>     name              geometry #> 1 Lisbon POINT (-9.139 38.722) #> 2  Porto  POINT (-8.611 41.15)

title: Compare two coordinate reference systems without PROJ — geo_crs_equal
text: "identical": absent, string byte byte, PROJJSON object ignoring key order. zugeo's checks use level. "structural": PROJJSON compared dropping members change coordinates ($schema, name, remarks, usages, scope, area, bbox) treating integers doubles alike. string CRS identical gives NA. "authority": authority code, AUTHORITY:CODE string PROJJSON id, authority's case ignored pairs differ axis order (OGC:CRS84 EPSG:4326) treated one. side authority code gives NA. NA means zugeo tell without PROJ, never two differ.
